newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent eases, other N. Sea crudes edge higher.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent eases, other N. Sea crudes edge higher.

text.p: North Sea crudes were mixed on Friday as cash Brent eased and the first September barrels of other grades looked to improve on differentials achieved for late August cargoes, traders said.
Benchmark Dated Brent was broadly steady amid talk that a second Aug 28-30 cargo trading at Sept Brent -9 cents after an early deal at -8 cents, but some said the grade was heading for a fall.
Brent CFDs for next week's Aug 18-22 dates traded at Oct Brent -26 cents, six cents weaker than early trade and cash intermonth spreads also backed off.
The Sept/Oct spread fetched -7 cents, five cents weaker than trade late on Thursday. Oct Brent on the IPE shed 12 cents to $18.94 a barrel by 1530 GMT.
One Brent cargo was due to turn wet on Friday, traders said.
Elsewhere in the North Sea, sellers were drawing modest encouragement from evidence of thinner loadings next month.
Schedules released this week showed volumes from the eight main export systems were expected to fall by 280,000 barrels per day (bpd).

Norwegian Oseberg, which should see volumes increase next month after returning from maintenance in August, fetched a firmer premium on Friday as one million barrels due to load Sept 4-6 traded at Dated Brent +25 cents.
A late August cargo traded at +15 cents on Thursday.
Other Norwegian crudes, particularly the offshore loaders with fixed shipping costs, were looking even better placed as local freight rates surged, traders said.
Shipping brokers reported at least four fixtures for Aframax vessels at 135 Worldscale points for northwest European trips, up about 20 points.
